thirtyTwoBitSupportRationale: minSdk 26 still admits 32-bit-only Android 8 and 9 devices. Per-ABI splits cut the download for everyone without cutting those devices off, so 32-bit ships and is declared rather than being quietly present under a 64-bit-only claim. Dropping armeabi-v7a and x86 is a separate user-facing decision.

abiSplitEvidence.note: Measured while FFmpeg still shipped: per-ABI splits cut the download from 199 MB to 60 MB on the architecture every modern phone uses. That was above IzzyOnDroid's 30 MB per-APK ceiling. See ffmpegRemovalEvidence for the size after FFmpeg left the APK.

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.implementation: Media3 Transformer owns clipping, PCM fades, pitch-preserving speed, M4A, WAV, and device-supported OGG or Opus exports. jump3r encodes MP3, Aura's own encoder writes FLAC, and lossless MP3 and FLAC cuts copy frames in Kotlin.

tests.wavTrimFade: A one-second 8 kHz PCM fixture is trimmed to 600 ms, given exact 200 ms linear fades, and compared sample for sample against 4,800 expected PCM values.
tests.wavSpeed: A one-second 440 Hz PCM fixture exports at 2x in 490 to 510 ms while the detected pitch remains between 420 and 460 Hz.
tests.aacConvert: A one-second WAV fixture exports as audio/mp4a-latm at 192 kbps within a 975 to 1,025 ms duration window.

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.artifactBuild: The final signed public artifacts were rebuilt with optional provider BuildConfig defaults blank, then scanned against the workstation values before measurement.
mediaStackMigrationEvidence.sizeFinding: FFmpeg still shipped at this point, so each FOSS split grew by 152,465 bytes and each full split grew by 156,597 to 156,601 bytes for this delivery.

legacyPackagingDecision.reason: youtubedl-android still expands its zipped Python payload at runtime for stream extraction.

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.videoEditingStatus: Video crop, Fit Canvas and HLS downloads run on Media3. FFmpeg no longer ships. The yt-dlp runtime is what keeps Python in the APK.

ffmpegRemovalEvidence.note: Release builds with no libffmpeg.zip.so in any ABI. Every per-ABI APK is under IzzyOnDroid's ceiling now; the universal APK isn't, and it isn't what that listing would use.

nestedArchiveEvidence.note: The gate used to record lib/<abi>/*.zip.so as skipped, so roughly 250 shipped 64-bit ELFs per ABI were never measured. It now reads inside those archives. Measured against APKs assembled from the exact io.github.junkfood02.youtubedl-android 0.18.1 ffmpeg and library AAR payloads, because no release APK could be built on this host.
nestedArchiveEvidence.finding: Every 64-bit LOAD segment in the Python payload is 16384. The libwebp objects that used to fall short came in with FFmpeg and left with it.
